question.value: Are molecular cloud physical properties and SFRs comparable between the inner Milky Way and nearby galaxies when observed at matched resolution, and how do internal clumps relate to cloud star-forming potential

evidence.quote: When observed at similar spatial and velocity resolutions, molecular clouds in the same mass range across these galaxies show broadly comparable physical properties and similar star formation rates (SFRs).
If we aim to use molecular clouds in the Milky Way as a benchmark, we must first establish their comparability to those in nearby galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Milky Way and nearby-galaxy molecular clouds have comparable properties and SFRs
claims.experiment: Identify clouds in three PHANGS galaxies and the inner Milky Way, smooth Milky Way clouds to 53.5 pc, compare properties and SFRs
claims.result: Properties and SFRs are broadly comparable at matched resolution
claims.finding: Clouds in the same mass range are comparable, but only after smoothing to extragalactic resolution

evidence.quote: molecular clouds in the same mass range across these galaxies show broadly comparable physical properties and similar star formation rates (SFRs)

claims.hypothesis: The beam effect biases radius, density and virial parameter in extragalactic observations
claims.experiment: Compare original high-resolution Milky Way clouds (r_t) with smoothed ones (r_s)
claims.result: Column density-mass correlation after smoothing is an artifact; clouds below N0 ~ 10^20.9 cm^-2 are beam-affected
claims.finding: Criteria derived to exclude beam-affected extragalactic clouds; properties then remain consistent

evidence.quote: The beam effect can artificially inflate cloud sizes, leading to inaccurate estimates of radius, density, and virial parameters.

claims.hypothesis: Some NGC 5236 clouds differ from the Milky Way in velocity dispersion
claims.experiment: Compare velocity dispersions after the beam-effect filter
claims.result: A small fraction of NGC 5236 clouds show higher velocity dispersions
claims.finding: Possibly due to environmental effects such as the bar and spiral arms

evidence.quote: This may reflect the influence of the galactic environment.

claims.hypothesis: Milky Way clouds with and without clumps differ, and cloud mass regulates internal clump properties
claims.experiment: Match ATLASGAL clumps to clouds, split into two groups, correlate cloud mass with clump mass, number and most massive clump
claims.result: Clump-associated clouds are more massive, denser, higher velocity dispersion, lower virial parameter, stronger 8 um; strong correlations with clump quantities
claims.finding: A cloud's physical conditions regulate its internal clump properties and star-forming potential

evidence.quote: These results suggest that a cloud’s physical conditions regulate its internal clump properties and, in turn, its star-forming potential.

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparability is partly built in by the smoothing recipe and the empirical r_s rules; the four-case radius assignment is ad hoc and untested against actual smoothed cubes
Different CO lines (2-1 vs 1-0, 12CO vs 13CO) and a single constant X_CO are used across samples with no line-ratio or metallicity treatment
Cloud definitions differ between dendrogram on 2D maps (galaxies) and on l-v maps (Milky Way), so cloud complexes are not equivalent populations
Galaxy sample is only three galaxies, one of which (NGC 2835) has 130 clouds
No uncertainties are given on the fitted mass relations
